mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 3.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the discount rate for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 3.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which triggers risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 5.5% (or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not negative in > 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.5% (or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window).

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock (indicated by a monthly decline in industrial production exceeding 1.0%), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns due to heightened recession risks and reduced corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of supply shock instances (INDPRO decline > 1.0%) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above their 12-month moving average signal a robust housing market, which correlates with strong consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI reading above 3.0% signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to consider rate hikes and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% (or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in payroll employment and rising unemployment rates indicate a deteriorating labor market, which triggers equity sell-offs and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decline > 0.5% and UNRATE rise > 0.2pp from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not negative in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS declines > 0.5% and UNRATE rises > 0.2pp (or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS above 4.5% and rising), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns due to higher borrowing costs and reduced corporate investment.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of monetary tightening cycle instances (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.
